mcq.q: Which type of entrepreneur copies existing products made by innovators and imitates their technology, process and methods?
mcq.e: The imitating entrepreneur copies the innovative entrepreneur's products, technology, process and methods.

mcq.q: Which entrepreneur is skeptical about change and waits for the outcome of released products in the market before starting the next project?
mcq.e: The Fabian entrepreneur is skeptical about change and waits to see how released products fare.

mcq.q: Which entrepreneur is happy with business results even with financial losses and is reluctant to make any change?
mcq.e: The drone entrepreneur is reluctant to change and content with results even when they involve financial losses.

mcq.q: Which entrepreneur has a great passion for discovering new products, ideas and processes and enjoys the challenge of risk?
mcq.e: The innovative entrepreneur is passionate about discovering new products, ideas and processes and enjoys risk.

mcq.q: Entrepreneurship is described as "creating the new and destroying the old." Which of these is NOT listed as something new?
mcq.e: Taxes are not on the slide's list of new things (knowledge, products, processes, services, markets, business models, raw materials). The closest wrong options, new business models and new raw materials, are both on that list.

mcq.q: According to Kuratko and Hodgetts (2007), an entrepreneur is an innovator who recognizes opportunities, adds value, and also:
mcq.a: Assumes the risks of the competitive marketplace and realizes the rewards
mcq.e: Kuratko and Hodgetts describe the entrepreneur as one who assumes the risks of the competitive marketplace and realizes the rewards.

mcq.q: A technopreneur is defined by Daniel Mankani (2003) as an entrepreneur who:
mcq.a: Uses cutting-edge technology to develop a new business
mcq.e: Mankani (2003) defines a technopreneur as an entrepreneur who uses cutting-edge technology to develop a new business.

mcq.q: Technopreneurship is best described as:
mcq.e: Technopreneurship is entrepreneurship in a technology-intensive context, merging technology prowess with entrepreneurial skills.

mcq.q: Technology Developers, who create unique technology capable of driving a new business, are also known as:
mcq.e: Technology developers who create unique technology are the inventors, since the notes equate inventors with developers. The closest confusion is innovators, which is the name for technology users.

mcq.q: Technology Users, who see a new technology and apply it to meet a new market need, are also known as:
mcq.e: Technology users who see a new technology and apply it to a new market need are the innovators. The closest confusion is inventors, which is the name for technology developers.

mcq.q: Which is NOT considered a technology-based enterprise even though it uses computers?
mcq.e: An internet cafe uses computers in its operations but is not a technology-based enterprise, which must gain competitive advantage from direct or indirect use of technology. The closest confusion is the iPod maker or software startup, which are technology-based.

mcq.q: The slide cites which Apple innovation as a technopreneurship example with a 160 GB, 1.8-inch hard disk drive?
mcq.e: The 160 GB, 1.8-inch hard disk drive is the iPod's innovation in the slides. The closest confusion is the iPad or MacBook, which the slides do not cite for this example.

mcq.q: Which company is cited for offering one-day delivery anywhere in the world through its sorting and delivery facility?
mcq.e: UPS is the slide's example of one-day delivery anywhere in the world.

mcq.q: How many stages are in the technopreneurial process shown in the slides?
mcq.e: The technopreneurial process has 8 steps, from idea generation to monitoring and evaluation. The closest confusion is 5, which is the number of steps in the entrepreneurial process.

mcq.q: Which is the FIRST step of the technopreneurial process?
mcq.e: Idea generation is step 1 of the technopreneurial process.

mcq.q: Which is the LAST step of the technopreneurial process?
mcq.e: Monitoring and evaluation is step 8, after commercialization.

mcq.q: In the technopreneurial process, which step comes right after concept testing?
mcq.e: Business analysis is step 4 and comes directly after concept testing (step 3). The closest confusion is prototyping, which is step 5 and comes after business analysis.

mcq.q: The 5 steps of the entrepreneurial process end with:
mcq.e: The entrepreneurial process ends with scaling and harvesting (step 5).

mcq.q: Innovation that happens incrementally, as a response to customer and market demands, is called:
mcq.e: Sustaining innovation is incremental and responds to customer and market demands.

mcq.q: Another name for sustaining innovation is:
mcq.e: The notes give routine innovation as the other name for sustaining innovation. Radical, frontier and reverse innovation are not listed as alternative names for it.

mcq.q: Which companies are cited as examples of sustaining innovation?
mcq.e: The slides cite Apple, Intel and Amazon as sustaining innovators. The closest confusion is the Kodak, Nokia and Sears set, which the notes do not cite as sustaining examples.

mcq.q: Who popularized the idea of disruptive innovation?
mcq.e: Clayton Christensen popularized disruptive innovation.

mcq.q: Which Clayton Christensen book was published in 1997?
mcq.e: Christensen's The Innovator's Dilemma was published in 1997. The closest confusion is The Innovator's Solution, the follow-up book, which is not the 1997 title.

mcq.q: A classic example of disruptive innovation given in the slides is:
mcq.e: Cellphones displacing fixed-line telephony is the slides' classic disruptive example.

mcq.q: Innovation that comes from inside a company and pushes something to the next level, opening new markets, is called:
mcq.e: Breakthrough innovation comes from inside a company, pushes something to the next level and opens new markets.

mcq.q: Which product is the slide's example of breakthrough innovation?
mcq.e: The slides use the Apple iPhone as the breakthrough example.

mcq.q: Innovation that begins with the discovery of a new phenomenon and seeks to understand how nature and people are put together is:
mcq.e: Basic research starts with discovering a new phenomenon to learn how nature and people are put together.

mcq.q: Which principle of sustainable innovation states that new products must solve real customer problems?
mcq.e: Value creation means new products must solve real customer problems. The closest confusion is ownership or accountability, which are other principles in the list of ten.

mcq.q: Which principle says that team members and leaders have full responsibility and obligation in the innovation?
mcq.e: Accountability means the team and leaders carry full responsibility for the innovation. The closest confusion is ownership, where the business leader owns the new products.

mcq.q: Which principle says that achieving the ROI should be followed by incentives for employees?
mcq.e: Net result and reward means that when ROI is achieved, employees get incentives. The closest confusion is observe and measure, which tracks ROI but does not itself give incentives.

mcq.q: "Technopreneurs are risk takers" matches which principle for sustainable innovation?
mcq.e: "No risk, no innovation" is the principle that technopreneurs are risk takers.

mcq.q: In idea selection, the "ABC analysis" is used in which step?
mcq.e: Rough selection, the first of three idea-selection steps, uses ABC analysis.

mcq.q: In the ABC analysis, which ideas are discussed and decided on together?
mcq.e: B-ideas are uncertain, so they are discussed and decided together.

mcq.q: In the ABC analysis, C-ideas are:
mcq.e: C-ideas have no value and are rejected.

mcq.q: In the "dots gluing" method of fine selection, how many sticky points does each participant receive?
mcq.e: In dot gluing each participant gets 5 sticky points to distribute among ideas. The closest confusion is the rating method, which uses a 0 to 5 point scale instead.

mcq.q: When there are fewer than ten ideas, fine selection can use the "rating" method with points from:
mcq.e: When there are fewer than ten ideas, each participant rates every idea from 0 to 5 points. The closest confusion is dot gluing, which gives each participant 5 sticky points.

mcq.q: Which is a criterion used in the detailed analysis of product ideas?
mcq.e: Detailed analysis judges customer benefit, differentiation and competitive factor, and technical and economic feasibility.

mcq.q: A canvas by which person can be used in detailed analysis for new business models?
mcq.e: Osterwalder's canvas can be used in detailed analysis for new business models.

mcq.q: A focus group typically consists of how many people with a moderator?
mcq.e: A focus group is typically 8 to 12 people led by a moderator. The notes give this as the size, so the other size ranges in the options do not match.

mcq.q: The researcher gathers information by simply watching how a subject interacts with a product. This technique is:
mcq.e: Observation means watching how a subject interacts with a product.

mcq.q: A one-on-one interview using probing questions to understand a person's product preferences is a(n):
mcq.e: An in-depth interview is one-on-one with probing questions.

mcq.q: Determining whether your product is of interest to a target market, usually before significant investment, is called:
mcq.e: Market validation checks whether a target market is interested in your product, usually before significant investment.

mcq.q: What is the FIRST of the 5 steps to determine market validation?
mcq.a: Write down goals, assumptions and hypotheses
mcq.e: Step 1 of market validation is writing down goals, assumptions and hypotheses. The closest confusion is assessing market size and share, which is step 2.

mcq.q: Which is the LAST of the 5 steps of market validation?
w: Research search volume of related terms
mcq.e: Step 5, the last step, is testing the product or service with alpha and beta testing.

mcq.q: Testing by internal employees in a staged setting to eliminate bugs before outside users see the product is:
mcq.e: Alpha testing uses internal employees in a staged setting to remove bugs before outsiders see the product.

mcq.q: Testing by a limited group of real external users who are told to identify problems is:
mcq.e: Beta testing uses a limited group of real external users told to find problems.

mcq.q: Which stage of the decision-making process comes right after "Information search"?
mcq.e: Information search is followed by evaluation of alternatives (stage 3). The closest confusion is the selection stage, which comes after evaluation of alternatives.

mcq.q: The 5th and last stage of the decision-making process is:
mcq.e: The five stages end with evaluation of the decision.

mcq.q: The Business Model Canvas was proposed by:
mcq.e: Alexander Osterwalder proposed the Business Model Canvas (the slides also follow Alex Cowan's explanation).

mcq.q: How many building blocks does the Business Model Canvas have?
mcq.e: The Business Model Canvas has 9 building blocks.

mcq.q: Which BMC block answers "Who are the customers? What do they think, see, feel, do?"
mcq.e: Customer segments asks who the customers are and what they think, see, feel and do.

mcq.q: A media property such as CNN.com with readers on one side and advertisers on the other is an example of a:
mcq.e: CNN.com serves readers and advertisers, which makes it a multi-sided market.

mcq.q: Which BMC block is "the value a company promises to deliver to customers should they choose to buy"?
mcq.e: The value proposition is the value the company promises to deliver to customers.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the five phases of channels?
mcq.e: The five channel phases are awareness, evaluation, purchase, delivery and after sales. Production is not a channel phase; it belongs to the key activities block.

mcq.q: In the channel phases, "word of mouth, social media, newspaper, television and flyers" belong to which phase?
mcq.e: Word of mouth, social media, newspapers, TV and flyers are awareness channels.

mcq.q: Which are the 3 benefits of good customer relationships listed in the slides?
mcq.e: Good customer relationships bring retention, loyalty and satisfaction.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a way to generate revenue streams listed in the slides?
mcq.e: Crowdfunding is a way to raise startup capital, not one of the revenue streams (product sale, usage, subscription, lending/renting/leasing, brokerage, advertising, volume and unit selling). The closest confusion is the funding-source list, where crowdfunding does appear.

mcq.q: Which BMC block asks "What can the company not do so it can focus on its key activities?"
mcq.e: The slide's key partnerships block is described as what the company will not do itself, so it can focus on key activities.

mcq.q: A strategic alliance between competitors is called:
mcq.e: Coopetition is cooperation between competitors, which is listed under key partnerships. The closest confusion is joint venture, another key-partnership type, but the notes place strategic alliances among non-competitors.

mcq.q: According to the slides, what percent of Google's revenue comes from advertising?
mcq.e: The slides say 97% of Google's revenue comes from advertising. The closest confusion is the 50% or 75% options, which the notes do not give for Google.

mcq.q: A cost structure focused on creating more value in the product rather than the lowest cost is:
mcq.e: Value-driven cost structures focus on creating more value in the product rather than the lowest cost.

mcq.q: A cost structure focused on minimizing costs of the product or service is:
mcq.e: Cost-driven cost structures focus on minimizing the cost of the product or service.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a type of key resource listed in the slides?
mcq.e: The key resource types are physical, intellectual, human and financial; political is not one.

mcq.q: Patents, brands, copyrights and customer lists are what kind of key resources?
mcq.e: Patents, brands, copyrights and customer lists are intellectual resources.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the five types of intellectual property rights?
mcq.e: A franchise is a business arrangement, not one of the five IP types (copyright, patents, trade secrets, trademarks, industrial design). The closest confusion is trademark, which is one of the five.

mcq.q: Which IP right protects literary and artistic works, including computer programs and databases?
mcq.e: Copyright protects literary and artistic works, including computer programs and databases.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a right granted under copyright law?
mcq.e: Patenting an invention is a patent right, not a copyright right; copyright covers reproducing, derivative works, distributing, and public performance and display. The closest confusion is performing the work publicly, which is a copyright right.

mcq.q: Patent applications in the Philippines are published in the:
mcq.e: Philippine patent applications are published in the IPO Gazette, where anyone may contest them. The closest confusion is the Official Gazette of the BIR, which is not the patent publication.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a type of patent mentioned in the slides?
mcq.e: The slide patent types are utility, design and plant; a process falls under utility.

mcq.q: A patent covering an original, new and ornamental design for a manufactured product is a:
mcq.e: A design patent covers an original, new and ornamental design.

mcq.q: A practice or process generally unknown outside the company that gives an economic advantage is a:
mcq.e: A trade secret is a practice or process not generally known outside the company that gives it an economic advantage.

mcq.q: A special trademark that designates protection for services is a:
mcq.e: A service mark protects services, which are non-product items, while trademarks identify products. The closest confusion is the collective mark (owned by an organization) and the certification mark.

mcq.q: A special trademark owned by an organization or association is a:
mcq.e: A collective mark is owned by an organization or association. The closest confusion is the service mark, which protects services, and the certification mark, which ascertains adherence to regulations.

mcq.q: A mark registered to ascertain adherence to local regulations is a:
mcq.e: A certification mark is registered to ascertain adherence to local regulations. The closest confusion is the trademark, which distinguishes products, and the collective mark, which is owned by an organization.

mcq.q: The ornamental or aesthetic aspect of an article, including 3D shape or 2D patterns, is covered by:
mcq.e: Industrial design protects the ornamental or aesthetic aspect of an article, in 3D shape or 2D patterns.

mcq.q: Which investors make high-risk investments in early-stage ventures as individuals?
mcq.e: Angel investors are individuals making high-risk investments in early-stage ventures.

mcq.q: Which investors invest in relatively mature ventures with a track record in a 1–5 year time frame?
mcq.e: Private equity firms invest in relatively mature ventures with a track record, on a 1-5 year time frame. The closest confusion is angel investors, who make high-risk investments in early-stage ventures.

mcq.q: Which source of funds offers the lowest cost of capital according to the slides?
mcq.e: The slides say banks offer the lowest cost of capital.

mcq.q: Strategic investors are usually:
mcq.a: Larger companies in the same industry
mcq.e: Strategic investors are usually larger companies in the same industry.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a way of raising capital for startups listed in the slides?
mcq.e: Issuing government bonds is not one of the five listed ways to raise startup capital (own funding, crowdfunding, friends and family, loans, competitions). The closest confusion is crowdfunding, which is on that list.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a component of a small business financial plan?
mcq.e: A marketing slogan is not a component of a small-business financial plan; the components are statements, projections, ratios and break-even analysis. The closest confusion is the income statement and balance sheet, which are on the list.

mcq.q: Determining capital requirements and capital structure are objectives of:
mcq.e: Financial planning determines capital requirements and capital structure, among other objectives.

mcq.q: A document that summarizes operational and financial objectives with detailed plans and budgets is a:
mcq.e: A business plan summarizes operational and financial objectives with detailed plans and budgets.

mcq.q: How many sections are in the business plan outline in the slides?
mcq.e: The business plan outline has 7 sections, from the executive summary to the financial plan. The closest confusion is the other counts in the options, which do not match the outline.

mcq.q: Which section of the business plan comes FIRST?
mcq.e: The executive summary comes first in the outline.

mcq.q: Which section is the LAST in the business plan outline?
mcq.e: The financial plan is the 7th and last section.

mcq.q: How many blocks does the Lean Canvas have?
mcq.e: The Lean Canvas has 9 blocks, the same count as the Business Model Canvas but a different set. The closest confusion is the 9 blocks of the Business Model Canvas.

mcq.q: Which is a block of the Lean Canvas in the slides?
mcq.e: Unfair advantage is a Lean Canvas block. The closest confusion is key partnerships, customer relationships and key resources, which are Business Model Canvas blocks.

mcq.q: An elevator pitch is usually how long?
mcq.e: An elevator pitch is concise and usually lasts 30 seconds to 2 minutes. The closest confusion is 5 to 10 minutes, which is far longer than a pitch should be.

mcq.q: What is the FIRST step of the 5-step elevator pitch?
mcq.e: Step 1 of the pitch is introducing yourself with your name, company and service.

mcq.q: What is the LAST step of the 5-step elevator pitch?
mcq.a: Know when to stop and listen
mcq.e: Step 5 is knowing when to stop and listen.

mcq.q: Which of the three essential components of a pitch is the most important?
mcq.e: Stimulate interest is the most important of the three essential components of a pitch. The closest confusion is transition that interest and share a vision, which are the other two components.

mcq.q: The "100/20 Rule" is associated with which pitch component?
mcq.e: The 100/20 Rule is associated with the share a vision component (the value proposition). The closest confusion is stimulate interest, the other component the options name.

mcq.q: In the slide's list of 10 principles for sustainable innovation, which principle comes immediately after Ownership?
mcq.e: The order is Inspire, No risk no innovation, New product process, Ownership, Value creation, then Accountability (6th).

mcq.q: Which principle of sustainable innovation covers hiring, staffing training and continuous coaching?
mcq.e: Training and coaching is principle 7. Idea management (8) is about valuing customers' and sales members' input.

mcq.q: Which principle of sustainable innovation says to value customers' and sales members' input through brainstorming?
mcq.e: Idea management is principle 8. Observe and measure (9) is about tracking results such as ROI.

mcq.q: How many principles for sustainable innovation are listed in the slides?
mcq.e: The slides list 10 principles, from Inspire to Net result and reward.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the 10 idea-presentation styles in the slides?
mcq.e: The styles are storytelling, musical, video, photo-only, immersive, question, demonstrative, humorous, animated and props.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the 7 ways to generate revenue listed in the slides?
mcq.e: The seven are sale of physical product, usage fee, subscription fee, lending/renting/leasing, brokerage fees, advertising, and volume and unit selling.

mcq.q: How many ways to generate revenue does the slide list under revenue streams?
mcq.e: Seven ways are listed, from sale of a physical product to volume and unit selling.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the four key-activity groups in the Business Model Canvas slides?
mcq.e: The four groups are R&D, production, marketing, and sales and customer services.

mcq.q: Product and process selection, capacity, inventory and machine maintenance belong to which key-activity group?
mcq.e: These are listed under production. R&D covers new product research, existing product updates, quality checks and innovation.

mcq.q: Handling problems, assisting sales and clerical tasks belong to which key-activity group?
mcq.e: Sales and customer services covers handling problems, assisting sales and clerical tasks. Marketing covers strategy, research, communications and events.

mcq.q: Which investors have a mandate to fund ventures for economic, environmental, cultural or social-policy objectives?
mcq.e: Public funding agencies fund ventures for policy objectives and suit the early stage. Venture capital firms instead chase high returns on high-risk ventures.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the 6 types of investors in the slides?
mcq.e: The six are angel investors, public funding agencies, venture capital companies, private equity firms, strategic investors and banks.

mcq.q: Which financial-plan objective covers cash control, lending and borrowing?
w: Use scarce funds at least cost for maximum ROI
mcq.e: Framing financial policies covers cash control, lending and borrowing. Capital requirements are short and long term needs.

mcq.q: Determining the kind and proportion of capital is which objective of the financial plan?
mcq.e: Capital structure is the kind and proportion of capital; capital requirements are the short- and long-term amounts needed.

mcq.q: Which is NOT among the 6 listed points on the importance of a financial plan?
mcq.e: The slide's points include adequate funds, inflow/outflow balance, investor preference for planners, growth programs, reduced uncertainty, and stability and profitability.

mcq.q: How many components of a small-business financial plan are listed in the slides?
mcq.e: The eight include income statement, balance sheet, personnel plan, business ratios, cash-flow projection, income projections, assets and liabilities, and break-even analysis.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the 4 reasons for the importance of a business plan?
mcq.e: The four are raise money, make sound decisions, identify potential weaknesses and communicate your idea with stakeholders.

mcq.q: Which is the last of the 10 benefits of a business plan listed in the slides?
mcq.e: The list ends with strategic alignment, milestones, metrics and then realistic regular reminders.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the 4 final tips for the pitch?
mcq.e: The tips are take your time, make it conversational, avoid niche words and phrases, and express confidence.

mcq.q: In the 5-step pitch, which step comes immediately after identifying the problem your company solves?
w: Know when to stop and listen
mcq.e: The order is introduce yourself, identify the problem, announce your promise, offer proof and a plan, then know when to stop and listen.

mcq.q: Which pitch component addresses pain, fear or guilt and depends on logic?
mcq.e: Transitioning interest addresses pain, fear or guilt. Stimulating interest is the most important component; sharing a vision uses the 100/20 Rule.

mcq.q: In the slide's Lean Canvas, which block comes right after Problem?
mcq.e: The slide order is Problem, Customer Segments, Unique Value Proposition, Solution, Key Activity, Channels, Cost Structure, Revenue Streams, Unfair Advantage.

mcq.q: In the slide's Lean Canvas, which block is fifth?
mcq.e: Fifth is Key Activity, after Solution; the slide uses it where Ash Maurya's original has Key Metrics.

mcq.q: Which Lean Canvas block has no counterpart among the Business Model Canvas's blocks?
mcq.e: Problem (with Solution and Unfair Advantage) is unique to the Lean Canvas; the other options are blocks in both canvases.

mcq.q: Personas, single- versus multi-sided markets and current alternatives are discussed under which BMC block?
mcq.e: Customer Segments covers who the customers are, personas, problems, needs, habits and alternatives.

mcq.q: Which is NOT among the value proposition examples listed in the slides?
mcq.e: Listed examples include newness, performance, customization, design, brand/status, price, cost reduction, risk reduction and convenience.

mcq.q: Self-checkout, credit card and cash on delivery are examples of which channel phase?
mcq.e: They are purchase-phase channels. Delivery is over-the-counter or door-to-door; after sales is call center, return policy and assistance.

mcq.q: Which three core business types does the BMC propose in the slide wording?
mcq.e: The slide wording lists product, scope and infrastructure as the three core business types.

mcq.q: Which test may be opened to the public with an "unfinished" notice?
mcq.e: Beta testing uses real external users and may be public with an unfinished notice. Alpha testing is internal, by employees in a staged setting.

mcq.q: The "240 monthly searches" for "best mattress for lower back pain sufferers" (per Moz) supports which market-validation step?
mcq.a: Research search volume of related terms
w: Write down goals, assumptions and hypotheses
mcq.e: Step 3 researches search volume. Casper mattresses is the example for step 2, market size and share.

mcq.q: The slide contrasts the iPod's 160 GB, 1.8-inch drive with an average 3.5-inch drive of what capacity?
mcq.e: The average 3.5-inch drive in the slide held 40 GB, versus the iPod's 160 GB in a 1.8-inch drive.

mcq.q: Which definition of technopreneur is credited to Sarimah Hanim and Abd. Rashid (2008)?
mcq.a: An entrepreneur involved in technological changes in producing goods or services for his organization
w: An entrepreneur who uses cutting-edge technology to develop a new business
An entrepreneur who only sells technology products
An investor who funds technology startups
mcq.e: The cutting-edge technology definition belongs to Daniel Mankani (2003); Sarimah Hanim and Abd. Rashid stress technological changes in producing goods or services.

mcq.q: Who described innovation as a process of multiple activities by multiple actors in which new combinations of means and ends are developed, implemented and transferred?
mcq.e: This is Joerg Gemuenden's description. Barack Obama's quote instead describes innovation as creating something that improves the way we live our lives.

mcq.q: Which Clayton Christensen book is the follow-up to The Innovator's Dilemma?
mcq.e: The Innovator's Solution followed The Innovator's Dilemma (1997).

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the three basic requirements of a patent in the slides?
mcq.e: A patentable invention must be novel, inventive and industrially applicable; profitability is not a requirement.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the three conditions for a trade secret in the slides?
mcq.a: It is registered and published in the IPO Gazette
w: Its secrecy gives an economic benefit
mcq.e: A trade secret is not public, its secrecy gives economic benefit, and it is actively protected. Publication in the IPO Gazette applies to patent applications.

mcq.q: In the copyright application steps, what comes right after filling out the form?
mcq.a: Attach a copy of the work
w: Pay the filing fee at the IPO
mcq.e: The sequence is fill out the form, attach a copy of the work, then pay the filing fee at the IPO. Drawings and Gazette publication are for patents.

mcq.q: A process, article, machine or composition of matter is covered by which type of patent?
mcq.e: Utility patents cover process, article, machine and composition of matter. Design patents cover ornamental designs; plant patents cover new reproducible plants.

mcq.q: Patterns, lines and color of an article are which kind of industrial design?
mcq.e: 2D industrial design covers patterns, lines and color; 3D covers shape and surface.

mcq.q: Maps, technical drawings and advertisements are protected by which IP right?
mcq.e: Copyright covers literary and artistic works including maps, technical drawings and ads.
